config.why: Learn the why and the procedures stop being routines to memorise — they become applications of causes.

activities.anchor: The facial artery's course over the mandible
activities.caption: trigeminal or facial? file each fact
activities.name: dhNerveSort

config.prompt: Two nerves govern the dental visit — file each fact:

items.label: sensation to the face and teeth, through three divisions
the thin sheets of muscles of facial expression
the maxillary branch serving the upper teeth
the muscles behind a numb-patient's smile warning
the mandibular branch serving the lower teeth
the three divisions branching across the face

config.why: The trigeminal defines the injections; the facial nerve defines the warnings — anatomy is the map of every appointment.

activities.anchor: their ducts are where stones lodge
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the gland facts
activities.name: dhGlandSpot

config.prompt: One of these salivary-gland claims is backwards — click it:
lines: The parotid duct opens beside the upper second molar.
The submandibular gland sits under the floor of the mouth.
Saliva is the mouth's mineral supply line and its pH buffer.
Dry mouth matters mainly because speech becomes effortful.
Swollen lymph nodes are often the first sign that something systemic is present.
config.correction: Dry mouth is a caries accelerator and a Candida incubator — the mineral supply line and the pH buffer both go quiet at once.
config.why: The glands' clinical weight is chemical before it is mechanical: minerals, buffering, antimicrobials.

activities.anchor: a failure of fusion produces the cleft lip and palate
activities.caption: sequence tooth development
activities.name: dhToothDevOrder

config.prompt: From epithelium to eruption — put the stages in order:
items: A band of oral epithelium thickens and grows down into the jaw
Bud, cap and bell stages shape the enamel organ around a papilla
Ameloblasts secrete enamel outward while odontoblasts secrete dentin inward
Primary teeth mineralise before birth; permanent teeth follow in overlapping waves
config.why: Two cell lines meet and talk to each other — each tissue's formation signalling the other's — and the timeline is why fluoride dosing follows age.

activities.anchor: the reason a tooth responds to advancing decay by walling itself off
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the tooth's tissues
activities.name: dhTissueCloze

config.text: %%0%% — about 96 percent mineral — is the hardest tissue in the body, built of hydroxyapatite prisms. %%1%%, about 70 percent mineral, is living tissue threaded with tubules, and its odontoblasts survive for life. Around the root, %%2%% anchors the periodontal ligament that cushions chewing loads.
config.hint: The cap, the living middle, and the root's anchor.

activities.anchor: That explains the observation every clinician knows
activities.caption: true or false — the immunological reframing
activities.name: dhImmuneJudge

statements.s: The destruction in periodontitis is carried out mainly by the bacteria themselves.
statements.why: Mostly by the host's recruited inflammatory machinery — the reason damage varies enormously between patients with similar plaque.

statements.s: Two patients with similar plaque levels can suffer very different bone loss.
statements.why: The inflammatory response is the variable the clinician reads.

statements.s: Smoking and diabetes multiply periodontal risk.
statements.why: Both dysregulate inflammation and healing — hence 'risk multipliers'.

statements.s: The goal of therapy is sterilising the mouth.
statements.why: It is dysbiosis management: disrupt the biofilm, calm the inflammatory drive, control the multipliers.

activities.anchor: which is why their decay is so consequential
activities.caption: sequence the dentition timeline
activities.name: dhEruptionOrder

config.prompt: From before birth to the early twenties — order the milestones:
items: Primary teeth begin mineralising before birth
The twenty primary teeth erupt — roughly six months to three years
First permanent molars arrive behind the primary teeth — the six-year molars
The mixed dentition: primary and permanent coexisting, about six to twelve
The full thirty-two, including wisdom teeth, completes by the early twenties
config.why: Eruption timing is genuinely clinical knowledge — the mixed-dentition years are where sealants, fluoride dosing and orthodontic hygiene intersect.

activities.anchor: They matter for three reasons this lesson has already built
activities.caption: walk the parent's question
activities.name: dhBabyBranch

config.root: A parent asks whether a cavity in a three-year-old's molar can simply wait until the tooth falls out. Walk the answer.

start.text: What is happening beside and beneath that primary tooth right now?

choices.label: A permanent tooth is mineralising there — disease risks the successor
choices.feedback: The permanent teeth develop for years beside and beneath the primary ones — uncontrolled disease endangers the replacements.

choices.label: Nothing — the baby tooth is on its way out anyway
choices.feedback: Three reasons say otherwise — the next one is architectural.

space.text: And the primary tooth's other job in the arch?

choices.label: It reserves the room and steers the successor into place
choices.feedback: Plus the fluoride window falls exactly in childhood — dosing by age is a clinical skill, not a formality.

choices.label: It is a placeholder with no real function
choices.feedback: Reserving and steering is the function — early loss reshapes the arch.

done.text: Successor, space, and the fluoride window: three reasons the smallest teeth carry the largest stakes.

wrongway.text: The primary dentition is a working scaffold, not a disposable draft.

placeholder.text: Without the guide, the permanent tooth arrives into an arch that has already drifted.

config.why: Baby teeth matter three ways at once — and every reason comes from the sciences this lesson built.
